text.p: Greek construction firm TEB officials told institutional investors they expected 1996 pretax profits to fall 13.04 percent, down to 1.0 billion drachmas from 1.15 billion in 1995.
They also estimated 1996 turnover at 8.2 billion drachmas, up 26.9 percent from 6.46 billion in 1995.
They forecast 1997 profits will rise 3.65 percent to 1.1 billion drachmas.
TEB's orderbook of still incomplete projects is 50 billion drachmas, officials said.

The company is currently involved in the construction of the Elefsis-Stavros-Spata highway where it has a 6.9 percent participation and in the construction of the Rio-Antirio bridge, where it has a stake of 8.0 percent. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
